title: What's new in the hf CLI and huggingface_hub library
gist: Hugging Face recaps recent hf CLI and huggingface_hub updates: a deduplicated Xet cache, Jobs that can be triggered by webhooks, Storage Bucket downloads up to about 17x faster, and experimental Sandboxes for agents. The most notable data point is that 1 in 3 daily hf CLI users is an AI agent, and more than half of CLI uploaders work through an agent. A benchmark found the hf-cli skill cut agent turns by about a third without improving accuracy.

themes.theme: AI agents as primary CLI users

insights.claim: On a given day, 1 in 3 users of Hugging Face's hf CLI is an AI agent. For uploads, more than half of the users who upload to the Hub with the hf CLI do so through an AI agent.
insights.speaker: Célina Hanouti
insights.so_what: Agents are becoming the main users of developer tools. Platforms that design their tools for agents will capture more usage, which is a signal for developer-tool market positioning.
insights.quote: On a given day, 1 in 3 users of the hf CLI is an AI agent.

insights.claim: In a benchmark of 28 Hub tasks run through Hugging Face Inference Providers, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash and Kimi-K3 solved 99 to 100% of tasks with or without the hf-cli skill. With the skill, they needed about a third fewer turns and almost stopped calling --help.
insights.speaker: Célina Hanouti
insights.so_what: Agent skills save tokens and latency rather than improving capability, so their value is in cost per task, not in what agents can do.
insights.quote: The hf-cli skill makes them faster, not more accurate.

insights.claim: Recent models already know a lot about the hf CLI and find their way with hf --help, so they solve Hub tasks just as well without a dedicated skill. The skill mainly removes trial and error.
insights.speaker: Célina Hanouti
insights.so_what: This goes against the hype around skills and tool packs: well-documented CLIs may need little extra scaffolding for frontier and open models.
insights.locator: The hf-cli skill makes them faster

insights.claim: Hugging Face has built Jobs commands to suit scripts and agents. hf jobs stats prints a snapshot and exits, hf jobs logs without -f no longer hangs, and hf jobs run reconnects when the log stream drops.
insights.speaker: Célina Hanouti
insights.so_what: Shows that agent users are driving product design choices such as non-blocking, scriptable commands.

insights.claim: Hugging Face's experimental Sandboxes are isolated cloud machines, CPU or GPU and running any Docker image, that are built on Jobs. They are aimed at agents that need to run code they just wrote away from the user's laptop, and they support labels for tracking costs.
insights.speaker: Célina Hanouti
insights.so_what: Hugging Face is moving into agent code-execution infrastructure, competing with dedicated sandbox providers and expanding paid compute beyond hosting.
insights.quote: This is useful when an agent needs to run code it just wrote, away from your laptop.

insights.claim: Webhooks can now start a Hugging Face Job each time a watched repo or Storage Bucket changes, passing the event payload and secrets such as HF_TOKEN. This enables event-driven data and training pipelines on the Hub.
insights.speaker: Célina Hanouti
insights.so_what: Pushes the Hub toward being a full MLOps and pipeline platform, which makes customers stickier and increases compute consumption.

insights.claim: Hugging Face Jobs added retries, reruns with the same secrets and hardware, rescheduling, exposing ports on running jobs, and per-script Job config embedded in UV script headers.
insights.speaker: Célina Hanouti
insights.so_what: Production-grade job orchestration features point to Hugging Face competing for training and batch workloads.

insights.claim: Users can check their remaining ZeroGPU quota from the CLI or Python, so apps and agents built on ZeroGPU Spaces can warn users before they hit the daily limit. The example shows a base quota of 2,400 GPU-seconds.
insights.speaker: Célina Hanouti
insights.so_what: Free GPU access on Spaces is rationed, so exposing the quota helps steer heavy users toward paid tiers.

insights.claim: The Hugging Face cache now stores each Xet file once across repos and links to it instead of downloading it again. For example, FLUX.1-dev, FLUX.1-schnell and FLUX.1-Krea-dev all share the same 9.5 GB text encoder.
insights.speaker: Célina Hanouti
insights.so_what: Content-addressed storage via Xet cuts bandwidth and disk use, lowering costs for Hugging Face and its users as model variants multiply.
insights.locator: Shared cache: download each file once

insights.claim: HfFileSystem now downloads Xet files with hf_xet straight to disk. In a benchmark on HF Jobs, downloading a 2.15 GB parquet file fell from 2 minutes to about 7 seconds, and load_dataset in datasets 5.1.0 fell from 130 seconds to about 17.
insights.speaker: Célina Hanouti
insights.so_what: An order-of-magnitude faster data path makes Hugging Face Storage Buckets a credible alternative to cloud object storage for ML data.
insights.quote: downloading a 2.15 GB parquet file went from 2 minutes to about 7 seconds

insights.claim: hf download no longer makes one API call per file, which used to hit rate limits on repos with tens of thousands of files. In addition, 'from huggingface_hub import *' is now 6x faster, taking 0.39 seconds instead of 2.36.
insights.speaker: Célina Hanouti
insights.so_what: Small fixes to the developer experience, but they show repos growing to tens of thousands of files and API rate limits becoming a real constraint.
